title: BNCI 2025-002 Continuous 2D Trajectory Decoding dataset
description: This dataset comprises continuous 2D trajectory decoding from attempted arm movements recorded via 60-channel EEG from 10 participants (9 able-bodied, 1 with spinal cord injury) across 3 sessions. Participants performed motor imagery tasks including target-tracking (snakerun) and self-paced shape tracing (freerun) with visual feedback. The preprocessed data, acquired at 200 Hz and downsampled to 20 Hz, includes temporal features and source localization estimates suitable for regression-based brain-computer interface applications in neuroprosthetics and upper limb restoration.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 60 channels (actiCAP, Brain Products GmbH) at 200 Hz sampling rate with reference at right mastoid and ground at Fpz. Online anti-aliasing (25 Hz) and notch (50 Hz) filters were applied. Preprocessing included downsampling to 100 Hz, bad channel interpolation, eye artifact subtraction (SGEYESUB), removal of frontal channels, high-pass filtering (0.18 Hz), common average re-reference, pops and drifts attenuation (HEAR algorithm), low-pass filtering (3 Hz), and final downsampling to 20 Hz. Feature extraction employed temporal features (7 time points × 55 channels) and sLORETA source localization. Decoding used PLS regression with UKF smoothing.
